# Default workflow: plan, then delegate

Goal: reviewed, correct code by the shortest path. This session plans, writes tests and small changes, and checks results; free models write bulky code. Details: `/concord:plan-then-delegate`, `/concord:delegate`, `~/.claude/concord/`.

- Non-trivial change → `/concord:plan-then-delegate`: a one-page `PLAN_<ticket>.md` (never `PLAN.md`), open questions settled by the user, stop for approval, then run it as `/concord:delegate all` would.
- Plans shown for approval carry the schedule diagram and the critical-path ETA with its local clock time, never the sum of all phases (`/concord:plan-then-delegate` step 5).
- One ticket = one git worktree: `python3 ~/.claude/concord/wt.py new <TICKET>` from the main checkout, then `EnterWorktree`; write outputs inside it. After the user committed and pushed: `ExitWorktree keep`, then `wt.py done <TICKET>` outside the sandbox.
- Who writes code: this session for changes up to about 60 lines, code it already wrote while testing, and docs; a free model for bulky, well-specified work: `free-deepseek-flash`, then `free-glm-flash`, then `deepseek-flash` (Go allowance); all out → `concord:implementer-opus48`, said in one line. Paid `zen-*` only after asking. sonnet/haiku/opus only as the `concord:implementer` subagent (`~/.claude/concord/concord.py` enforces this).
- Tests first, by this session; implementers never edit tests. Delegated acceptance must fail on the untouched code (red run) unless marked `(characterization)`.
- Check a delegated phase yourself: the dispatcher's blocking report lines, its acceptance commands re-run, `git diff` of its files. A FAIL records its cause (EXECUTOR, PLAN_GAP, TEST_DEFECT, FLAKY, PROVIDER, BLOCKED); only EXECUTOR counts: three attempts with feedback, then ask.
- Checks are incremental (a pass re-runs only its phases' acceptance commands) until one full revision after the last pass: every suite (`tests/demo_test.sh` alone) and one review of the whole diff, by an independent agent (not the code's author): low = flash, medium and high = `concord:reviewer-opus55` (Claude subscription; say so in one line). With a PR it is the PR gate: until `concord.py --pr-status` prints REVIEWED for the current head, no PR, own or others', is called ready, mergeable or put in a merge order (GitHub "mergeable" is not a review). Without one, each implementing run's review, all at once. Fix confirmed BLOCKER/HIGH/MEDIUM findings right away (after reading the cited lines) and re-review the fix once (delta); still open after two fix rounds → ask. NOTE findings go in the report.
- Parallel by default: independent tickets, reviews and background runs at once, and a ticket in passes, not a chain (`/concord:plan-then-delegate` step 3). Only real dependencies wait: one writer per file and per checkout. Ask only for significant risk: irreversible or destructive actions, merges, publishing, outward writes not yet approved, spending beyond subscriptions and free tiers, or changing an owner decision, product behaviour or an eval set.
- Planner: the strongest model available, at high effort; else say so and ask before planning.
- Never commit; the user reviews the diff and commits.
- Tokens: auto-compact at a 400k window (`settings.snippet.json`); after a compaction re-read the ticket's plan. Chat and agent prose: terse. Plans, docs, commands, code, commit and PR text: full prose.
